title: NY State Assembly · District 38
area: Queens: Ozone Park, Woodhaven, South Richmond Hill, and parts of Jamaica

context.text: This is an open seat: in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, David Orkin defeated incumbent Assembly Member Jenifer Rajkumar 58.8% to 40.9%, so Rajkumar is not on the November ballot. The Republican primary was canceled and Ruben Cruz II (R) advanced without appearing on the ballot.

summary.text: David Orkin is an immigrant workers'-rights attorney and union organizer who defeated incumbent Jenifer Rajkumar in the June 2026 Democratic primary for the open Assembly District 38 seat.

background.text: Orkin holds a bachelor's degree from Vassar College (2013) and a law degree from CUNY School of Law (2022).
He has worked as an immigrant workers'-rights attorney at Make the Road NY, representing clients facing wage theft and employer abuse.

He is an elected member of the bargaining committee of his union, UAW Local 2320, where he helped negotiate a first contract that included raises of more than $10,000 for the lowest-paid staff, a free healthcare option, and a 35-hour workweek.
His mother immigrated from Tijuana, Mexico; he has organized against militarization of the Arizona-Mexico border and helped found the Tucson chapter of Jewish Voice for Peace.

priorities.text: "TAX THE RICH FOR AFFORDABILITY... As the richest New Yorkers and biggest corporations make more than ever, I'll fight for a state budget that asks them to pay their fair share in taxes to fund the services working people deserve: deeply affordable housing, universal childcare, guaranteed healthcare, fully funded public schools and free CUNY, world-class public transit, and more."

"PROTECT OUR IMMIGRANT NEIGHBORS. More than half of AD-38 residents are immigrants... In Albany, I'll fight to implement New York for All, ending collaboration between ICE & local law enforcement and protecting personal data from federal surveillance."

"STRENGTHEN WORKERS' RIGHTS... I'll champion the EmPIRE Worker Protection Act, which strengthens protections against wage theft, retaliation, unsafe workplaces, and union-busting. And I'll support a $30 minimum wage in New York."

summary.text: Ruben Cruz II is a small-business owner and community advocate running as the Republican and Queens United Party candidate for the open Assembly District 38 seat. He previously ran unsuccessfully for Assembly District 24 (2024) and State Senate District 16 (2022).

background.text: Cruz holds a bachelor's degree in Theatre and Dance from CUNY Queens College (1999) and is a graduate of Richmond Hill High School.
He is the founding director of a firm that has provided health, wellness, and arts and culture programming in New York City since 2006, and serves on Queens Community Board 9.
During the COVID-19 pandemic he founded the Queens Pet Pantry, a pet-supply distribution project; he says its data-management system was later adopted by the ASPCA.

priorities.text: On transit: "I will audit the MTA to bridge the... transit desert between Woodside and Woodhaven with reliable, eco-friendly bus service. We must address the alarming pollution levels in our subways to protect our health."

On homeowner protections: "I am fighting for economic justice for homeowners: I will legislate to ban property liens placed without owner knowledge and eliminate the hidden bank and utility fees that drain blue-collar paychecks."

On seniors and pets: "I am committed to preserving the rights of residents over 62 to live with their pets without housing discrimination and advocating for pet-friendly shelters so no neighbor is forced into homelessness to stay with a loved one."

researchNotes: Neither candidate has held elected office, so there is no official voting or bill-sponsorship record for either. Orkin's positions are documented in depth from his campaign's detailed platform statements and Ballotpedia survey. Cruz completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey with extensive priorities in his own words, but did not take clear stances on this guide's fixed issue list, so no Position entries are included for him; his research depth is marked 'basic' accordingly.
